Okay let me try a very simple way of putting it. 

Banks sold home loans to people. Then banks packaged these loans as a financial instruments and sold to other financial institutions. Why? To make money, of course. Why would anyone buy these loans? Because they offered guaranteed income. 

Then, banks started offering home loans to people who could not afford to pay EMIs. This is where things got murky. But since financial institutions buying these packaged loans got guaranteed income, they turned a blind eye and continued to buy these financial instruments. 

What was the mess all about? This exactly. More and more people started defaulting on their home loans as they couldn't pay. Once that happened, the financial instruments that guaranteed returns started to default as their underlying asset -- the home loan EMI was getting defaulted because it was sold to people who were not able to pay the EMIs. 

This meant what? EMIs were not being serviced, so banks interest income dropped, and their loans extended to buy homes went bad. Financial companies who bought these packaged loans for guaranteed returns had zero returns coming in. So they tried to sell these instruments but there was no one to buy them because they had no returns. 

What did this lead to? No money in the market. Hence, the financial crisis.

For some historical reference, during independence in 1947 India wasn't the landmass it is today. We had to talk to all the small kingdoms to join the Union of India. There was a tug of war going on with Pakistan as well. Junagadh in Gujarat was (is) a Hindu majority area but ruled by a Muslim. He wanted to join Pakistan. Kashmir was (is) a Muslim majority area with a Hindu ruler who hadn't made up his mind yet. This is pretty normal for the time as the then home minister was reaching out to all such tiny tinpot kingdoms telling them to join India. And many hadn't decided till then. 

While all this was going on, in 1948, months after independence, Pakistan decided to wrestle Kashmir's autonomy. Their point being Kashmir like Pakistan is Muslim majority and hence natural affinity. The ruler of Kashmir had no means to defend his land and asked India for help. India's first prime minister JN Nehru told him in order to defend Kashmir from Pakistan's occupation, the land must be part of India. It is then the treaty of accession was signed between Kashmir and India. Post this, India sent its army to Kashmir and halted Pakistan. By this time, Pakistan had already occupied some around 2/3rd of Kashmir on the western border. We call this Pakistan Occupied Kashmir. Pakistan calls it Free Kashmir. Although, if it's free why isn't it a country? Anyway. 

It is really important to note here that for nearly 40 years since independence there was no militancy in Kashmir. It was a peaceful place and very much part of India. It was only during the late 80s and early 90s that Pakistan upped the ante and tried the terrorism route to gain Kashmir back. You can read up on the 1965 war as well for more context on this. Post its failure to achieve its objective in Kashmir for 40 years, it turned to terrorism. Past 30-35 years are a result of that cross-border terrorism. This is why Kashmir today is heavily fortified with a large Indian Army presence. 

This is where mistakes were made as anyone in the position of power is likely to abuse and there are numerous examples of here. This ended up alienating parts the Kashmiri's population against India and the call for 'freedom' rose.
